column11: lookup.py seed Exagamglogene autotemcel: list_price_per_patient 2.2 mm USD, 'Vertex, Dec 2023 launch price' (Casgevy, the only marketed CRISPR/Cas9 therapy). Cross-check on HAE prophylaxis: Intellia management said payers value one-time therapies as a multiple of the average annual cost of long-term prophylaxis (LTP), which 'can exceed $700,000 annually'. No price has been set, and Intellia expects premium pricing (MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 'Intellia Eyes Lonvo-z Launch as HAE PDUFA Nears, TTR Study Advances', finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/intellia-eyes-lonvo-z-launch-040202231.html; read from the search summary, page not opened). Commercial plans paid a mean $395,845 per patient-year for LTP drugs (Tachdjian R et al., World Allergy Organ J 2026;19(7):101399, doi:10.1016/j.waojou.2026.101399, PMID 42318594; IQVIA PharMetrics Plus, 328 patients)
column12: JUDGEMENT on the anchor. Intellia has not set a price. Casgevy is the closest published price for the same modality: a one-time CRISPR/Cas9 therapy that replaces lifelong treatment. $2.2mm is 3.1 years of the more than $700,000 a year that management cites for LTP, and 5.6 years of the $395,845 commercial plans actually paid per patient-year. Case for higher: management expects premium pricing. Hemgenix, a one-time gene therapy that replaces hemophilia B prophylaxis, lists at $3.5mm, about 5 years of $700,000. Lonvo-z has no conditioning regimen and no hospital stay, and 62% of HAELO patients were attack-free and therapy-free for six months (8-K 0001193125-26-385194). Case for lower: HAE is rarely fatal, management says payer resistance rises at higher multiples and step edits are possible, durability past a few years is unproven, and newer LTPs (garadacimab, donidalorsen) add price competition. Casgevy's $2.2mm is carried by the book from a workbook cell; it matches Vertex's published December 2023 list price

column11: Zolgensma (onasemnogene abeparvovec, one-time IV gene therapy): the CMS reimbursement had fallen to $1.36mm by 2022 against a $2.125mm list price, which BioSpace calls 'nearly a 40% discount' ('Who's Paying for Million-Dollar Gene Therapies?', biospace.com/who-s-paying-for-million-dollar-gene-therapies; read from the search summary). 1 - 1.36/2.125 = 0.36
column12: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. The anchor is a list price (WAC), so neither house Medicare convention applies. The discount has to be sourced, and Zolgensma is the one-time gene therapy with a measured net-of-discount CMS figure against its list. Direction checked: 0.36 is the share off list, so net is $1.408mm per course. Case for lower: HAE patients are mostly commercially insured adults, while SMA infants carry a large Medicaid share. The Medicaid statutory minimum rebate is 23.1% of AMP and applies to Medicaid units only. The book's Casgevy seed assumes about 18% ($1.8mm net on $2.2mm, a workbook estimate). Case for higher: if $1.36mm is CMS's Part B payment limit (106% of ASP), the ASP-based discount is 1 - (1.36/1.06)/2.125 = 0.396

column11: Incumbent: Orladeyo (berotralstat), the last novel-mechanism HAE prophylaxis, launched December 2020. FY2025 net revenue was $601mm (BioCryst preliminary FY2025 release, ir.biocryst.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biocryst-announces-preliminary-full-year-2025-orladeyor), with 89.5% US (Q1 2025 release, above): $537.9mm. Divided by the $395,845 commercial plans paid per LTP patient-year (Tachdjian 2026, PMID 42318594), that is 1,359 US patient-years on therapy, 18.7% of Castaldo's 7,275 treated HAE patients, in Orladeyo's fifth year. Solved through the engine (forecast.derive_new_patients, k 1.08, midpoint 2.2, pool 6,049, inflow 61.5 a year) so that lonvo-z has treated 18.7% of the eligible pool by the end of year 5: p = 0.0828. Treated patients run 43, 109, 225, 345 and 408 a year, peaking at 418 in year 6
column12: JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 1.0 on Orladeyo's five-year share. Several steps are approximate. Revenue is net of rebates while $395,845 is the plan-paid amount, and 16% of Orladeyo patients were on free drug in Q1 2025 (search summary); both push the patient count up. Orladeyo users include normal-C1-INH patients, and its per-patient cost may exceed the all-LTP mean: berotralstat alone was about $312,559 per six months in persistent patients (Princic N et al., J Comp Eff Res 2025, doi:10.57264/cer-2024-0205, PMID 39976166), which gives 861 patient-years, an 11.8% share and p = 0.0511. The 2019 prevalence denominator predates later growth in treated HAE. Case for higher: 87% fewer attacks, 62% attack-free and therapy-free, and one treatment ends lifelong dosing. LTP churn is high: 12-month persistence was 58.7% in Komodo claims (Lumry W et al., Orphanet J Rare Dis 2026, doi:10.1186/s13023-026-04391-6, PMID 42157298), and Orladeyo took 257 of 499 LTP starts there. Case for lower: one-time gene therapies have launched slowly (the book's Casgevy seed peaks at 0.011), the edit is permanent, and management warns of payer step edits. New LTPs (garadacimab, donidalorsen, navenibart) are competing for the same switchers. Implied peak net revenue is about $588mm US ($657mm with ex-US) at the $1.408mm net price
